presentingComplaint: 3 days of worsening breathlessness with increased volume of thick green sputum in a man with severe COPD.
history: Ex-smoker (50 pack-years), GOLD group E severe COPD (FEV1 34% predicted) on triple inhaled therapy and home nebulisers. Four exacerbations in the past year with two hospitalisations; sputum culture 3 months ago grew Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and he completed a course of co-amoxiclav from a local clinic 2 weeks ago for a 'chest infection'. Over 3 days he reports increasing dyspnoea from baseline, a marked rise in sputum volume, and a change from clear to purulent green sputum with new wheeze. No pleuritic pain, no haemoptysis, no orthopnoea or leg swelling. Uses long-term home oxygen 2 L/min. No fever until today.
examination: Alert, tachypnoeic and using accessory muscles, speaking in short phrases. Barrel-shaped chest with prolonged expiratory phase, diffuse polyphonic wheeze and coarse crepitations at both bases. No focal consolidation on percussion. No raised JVP, no peripheral oedema, calves soft. Not cyanosed centrally; peripheries warm.

labs.abg_on_2L_O2: pH 7.33, PaCO2 7.4 kPa (55 mmHg), PaO2 8.1 kPa, HCO3 30 mmol/L, lactate 1.6 mmol/L

imaging: Chest X-ray: hyperinflated lung fields with flattened diaphragms and bullous change; no lobar consolidation, no effusion, no pneumothorax. Confirms exacerbation without new pneumonic infiltrate.
microbiology: Sputum Gram stain: many polymorphs, Gram-negative bacilli. Sputum culture at 48h: Pseudomonas aeruginosa, resistant to piperacillin-tazobactam and ceftazidime, susceptible to meropenem, cefepime and colistin (MDR phenotype). Blood cultures negative. Respiratory viral PCR negative.
differentialDiagnoses: Community-acquired pneumonia (excluded by absence of new infiltrate)
Acute heart failure / pulmonary oedema (no raised JVP, oedema or cardiomegaly)
Pulmonary embolism (no pleuritic pain, no risk factors, hypoxia explained by COPD)
finalDiagnosis: Acute infective exacerbation of COPD (Anthonisen type 1) due to MDR Pseudomonas aeruginosa, requiring escalation of empiric antipseudomonal therapy
citations: GOLD — Global Strategy for Diagnosis, Management and Prevention of COPD (2024)
Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine 22e — Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease
stewardship: This is an Anthonisen type 1 exacerbation (increased dyspnoea + sputum volume + sputum purulence) with respiratory failure, so antibiotics are indicated per GOLD alongside controlled oxygen, bronchodilators and systemic corticosteroids. Because of documented prior Pseudomonas isolation, frequent exacerbations, severe airflow limitation and recent antibiotic exposure, empiric cover must be antipseudomonal rather than a simple aminopenicillin/macrolide. Empiric piperacillin-tazobactam was started; sputum then grew an MDR Pseudomonas resistant to piperacillin-tazobactam and ceftazidime, mandating escalation to a carbapenem (meropenem) guided by susceptibilities, with airway clearance/physiotherapy as source control. Once the patient stabilises and cultures are back, de-escalate to the narrowest active agent (cefepime) and complete a 5-7 day course; review with respiratory microbiology/AMS.
contraindications: Avoid uncontrolled high-flow oxygen — titrate to SpO2 88-92% to prevent CO2 narcosis (baseline hypercapnia present)
Avoid non-antipseudomonal empiric antibiotics (e.g., amoxicillin, doxycycline) given prior Pseudomonas and MDR risk
Caution with carbapenem in any prior beta-lactam anaphylaxis; check penicillin allergy history
edgeCases: If pH <7.35 with rising PaCO2 despite therapy, start non-invasive ventilation
If sputum later grows carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas, escalate to colistin +/- combination therapy with AMS input
Colonisation vs infection: treat because of clear clinical exacerbation with purulence and neutrophilia, not sputum growth alone
expectedMaiK: Severe COPD with an Anthonisen type 1 infective exacerbation and hypercapnic respiratory failure; prior Pseudomonas plus recent antibiotics drive antipseudomonal empiric choice, and MDR resistance mandates carbapenem escalation with subsequent de-escalation.
